facts.text: A detection-testing trial should be defined as one independent approach event, not one camera frame.
facts.quote: Define a trial as one independent approach event, not one frame.

facts.text: A 10-second encounter producing 300 camera frames is one correlated encounter, not 300 independent detection opportunities.
facts.quote: A 10-second encounter producing 300 camera frames is one correlated encounter, not 300 detection opportunities

facts.text: Scoring detection by frame inflates the apparent sample size and makes confidence intervals grossly overconfident.
facts.quote: scoring by frame inflates the apparent sample size and makes confidence intervals grossly overconfident.

facts.text: For independent Bernoulli detection opportunities with zero misses, an exact one-sided claim follows from (1 - q)^n <= alpha, where q is the maximum miss probability, 1 - alpha is the desired confidence, and n is the number of independent opportunities.
facts.quote: For an independent Bernoulli detection opportunity with zero misses, an exact one-sided claim follows from (1 - q)^n <= alpha, where q is the maximum miss probability, 1 - alpha the desired confidence and n the number of independent opportunities.

facts.text: The zero-failure special case of exact binomial inference gives the required number of independent detection opportunities as n = ln(alpha) / ln(1 - q), where alpha is one minus the desired confidence and q is the maximum miss probability.
facts.quote: Solving gives n = ln(alpha) / ln(1 - q), the zero-failure special case of exact binomial inference.

facts.text: Demonstrating a miss rate at most 5% (detection at least 95%) with zero failures requires 59 independent trials at 95% one-sided confidence or 90 at 99% one-sided confidence.
facts.quote: | Miss rate at most 5% (detection at least 95%) | 0 | 59 | 90 |

facts.text: Demonstrating a miss rate at most 1% (detection at least 99%) with zero failures requires 299 independent trials at 95% one-sided confidence (about 300 by the rule of three) or 459 at 99% one-sided confidence.
facts.quote: | Miss rate at most 1% (detection at least 99%) | 0 | 299 (rule of three: about 300) | 459 |

facts.text: Demonstrating a miss rate at most 1% with one allowed failure requires about 474 independent trials at 95% one-sided confidence; the passage gives no trial count for 99% one-sided confidence.
facts.quote: | Miss rate at most 1% | 1 | about 474 | not given |

facts.text: Demonstrating a miss rate at most 1% with two allowed failures requires about 630 independent trials at 95% one-sided confidence; the passage gives no trial count for 99% one-sided confidence.
facts.quote: | Miss rate at most 1% | 2 | about 630 | not given |

facts.text: Demonstrating a miss rate at most 0.1% (detection at least 99.9%) with zero failures requires 2,995 independent trials at 95% one-sided confidence or 4,603 at 99% one-sided confidence.
facts.quote: | Miss rate at most 0.1% (detection at least 99.9%) | 0 | 2,995 | 4,603 |

facts.text: Demonstrating a miss rate at most 0.01% (detection at least 99.99%) with zero failures requires 29,956 independent trials at 95% one-sided confidence or 46,050 at 99% one-sided confidence.
facts.quote: | Miss rate at most 0.01% (detection at least 99.99%) | 0 | 29,956 | 46,050 |

facts.text: The detection sample-size table's zero-failure rows use exact binomial values.
facts.quote: Rows with zero failures are exact binomial values

facts.text: The detection sample-size table's rows allowing one or two failures use the Poisson or Clopper-Pearson approximation.
facts.quote: the rows with one or two failures use the Poisson or Clopper-Pearson approximation.

facts.text: A total of 2,995 physical runs does not establish sufficient evidence for an entire product family; 2,995 independent opportunities drawn from one clearly defined target population with zero misses support only an aggregate detection-at-least-99.9% claim at 95% confidence.
facts.quote: They mean that 2,995 independent opportunities drawn from one clearly defined target population with zero misses support that one aggregate 99.9%/95% statement.

facts.text: If a contractual or safety requirement demands separate 99.9% detection claims for rain, darkness, dust, each machine family and each scenario type, each claim needs adequate evidence of its own or a justified statistical pooling model.
facts.quote: If a contractual or safety requirement demands separate 99.9% claims for rain, darkness, dust, each machine family and each scenario type, each claim needs its own adequate evidence or a justified statistical pooling model.

facts.text: A claim of at most 1% misses in each of 20 critical strata needs about 6,000 independent zero-miss trials.
facts.quote: A claim of at most 1% misses in each of 20 critical strata needs about 6,000 independent zero-miss trials

facts.text: The allocation assessment considers about 6,000 independent zero-miss trials for 20 critical strata feasible only in simulation or hardware-in-the-loop.
facts.quote: about 6,000 independent zero-miss trials, which is only feasible in simulation or hardware-in-the-loop

facts.text: When simulation or hardware-in-the-loop supplies the large stratified detection trial count, physical tests should validate the simulation in each stratum and provide an independent, smaller-sample confirmation.
facts.quote: physical tests then serve to validate the simulation in each stratum and to give an independent, smaller-sample confirmation

facts.text: An example smaller-sample physical confirmation uses 59 trials per stratum for a detection bound of at least 95%.
facts.quote: for example 59 trials per stratum for a detection bound of at least 95%.

facts.text: If detection misses occur, use an exact binomial (Clopper-Pearson) interval or another pre-declared binomial interval rather than continuing testing until a desirable percentage appears.
facts.quote: If misses occur, use an exact binomial (Clopper-Pearson) interval or another pre-declared binomial interval rather than continuing until a desirable percentage appears.

facts.text: The Clopper-Pearson interval is exact and conservative and is the safe default for regulators.
facts.quote: Clopper-Pearson is exact and conservative and is the safe default for regulators

facts.text: The Wilson interval is less conservative than Clopper-Pearson and better behaved at moderate sample sizes.
facts.quote: the Wilson interval is less conservative and better behaved at moderate n.

facts.text: Estimation precision is distinct from demonstrating a detection-performance threshold.
facts.quote: A second distinction is estimation precision versus demonstrating a threshold.

facts.text: A generic 95% proportion estimate using worst-case variance needs about 9,604 independent observations for precision of plus or minus 1 percentage point.
facts.quote: A generic 95% proportion estimate with worst-case variance needs about 9,604 independent observations for plus or minus 1 percentage point

facts.text: A generic 95% proportion estimate using worst-case variance needs about 38,415 independent observations for precision of plus or minus 0.5 percentage point.
facts.quote: about 38,415 for plus or minus 0.5 point.

facts.text: Near a proportion of 99%, variance is smaller than the worst-case variance, and exact interval design should replace the worst-case sample-size approximation.
facts.quote: Near 99% the variance is smaller, and exact interval design should be used instead of the worst-case approximation.
